question.question: A process is running with a priority of 20. How will the Linux scheduler handle this process compared to a process with a priority of 10?

options.text: The process with priority 20 will always run before the process with priority 10
The process with priority 20 will run before the process with priority 10, but only when the system is under heavy load
The process with priority 20 will run before the process with priority 10, but only when both processes are competing for the same CPU core
The process with priority 20 will run after the process with priority 10

question.explanation: In Linux, higher priority processes are scheduled before lower priority processes. This ensures that critical tasks are completed promptly, even in the presence of other processes competing for resources.
